hook: Martin Luther, an Augustinian friar, posts theses against the sale of indulgences

segments.voice: Yesterday, Florence, a reunion signed but not received. Your line was almost one. Today a new split begins, this time inside the West.

A preacher arrives near a small university town in Germany, raising money to rebuild Saint Peter's in Rome and offering indulgences to those who give. People cross the border to hear him. In that town, a friar of the Augustinian order, who teaches scripture at the university and hears confessions, is troubled by what his penitents tell him. He sits down and writes a list of theses for debate. He's not trying to start a new church. He wants an argument about penance. Today's word is Reformation.
screen: `A PREACHER OFFERS INDULGENCES.` → `A FRIAR HEARS CONFESSIONS.` → `A LIST FOR DEBATE.`

segments.voice: First, the question. An indulgence, in Catholic teaching, is a remission of temporal punishment for sins already forgiven, granted by the Church. What troubled Martin Luther was the selling: the impression that a coin could do what only repentance and grace could. Next, his very first thesis, which goes back to Jesus. In Matthew, Jesus begins to preach, and in the Douay-Rheims he says, "Do penance, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand." Luther wrote that when Christ said this, he meant the whole life of believers to be one of penance. Not a transaction: a whole life turned around. Then, the door. The story often told is that he nailed the theses to the church door at Wittenberg. Some historians doubt the hammer. The list itself is not in doubt: he sent it to his archbishop, and printers spread it. Finally, what it became. Luther hoped for a debate. What followed was a break, deeper and longer than anyone at the time planned, with faults and hard words on more than one side. Today Catholics and Lutherans speak of this history together, and a pope has prayed alongside Lutheran leaders to remember it. Catholic tradition says the Church is always in need of purification, and the friar's first thesis was about exactly that. Strictly he was a friar, not a monk, but the line holds: it began as a call to turn around.
screen: `AN INDULGENCE, AND ITS SALE.` · `THE WHOLE LIFE, PENANCE.` · `A DOOR, A LIST, A PRESS.` · `A DEBATE BECOMES A BREAK.` · then, large: `A MONK WANTED REFORM.`

segments.voice: Picture two churches on one street, one Catholic and one Lutheran, their bells ringing on the same Sunday, and hold both congregations in view: the families, the old people in the front pews, the children. Wish them both well, honestly and without picking. If you pray, use the prayer both say, the Our Father, slowly, once for each.
Reformation. The movement that began with a friar's call to reform the Church, and became a lasting division in the West. Today's word.
Your line: a monk wanted reform. It started with turning, not leaving. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Catholics and Lutherans today hold joint services and dialogue about their shared history; in Catholic teaching indulgences still exist, but their sale is forbidden.

chat.says: Did Luther set out to start his own church?
options: No: he wanted a debate on penance; the break that followed went far beyond his plan.
Yes: he nailed up the theses to announce a new church, separate from Rome.
No: he only wanted the Bible printed in German, and the theses were about that.
chat.meaning: Luther's first thesis called the whole life of believers one of penance. He hoped for a debate; the break went deeper than anyone planned.

notes: Year 1517 is in the index title only; not spoken. The number of theses is not stated.
The preacher is Johann Tetzel (not named); 'people cross the border to hear him' (indulgence preaching was banned in Electoral Saxony): confirm.
Definition of an indulgence follows CCC 1471; confirm wording.
Thesis 1 paraphrased from the Latin; confirm.
'Sent to his archbishop' (Albrecht of Mainz): confirm.
'A pope has prayed alongside Lutheran leaders to remember it' refers to Pope Francis at Lund (2016); confirm phrasing.
'Catholic tradition says the Church is always in need of purification' paraphrases Lumen Gentium 8 (semper purificanda); confirm.
Index carry says 'monk'; Luther was an Augustinian friar. The script keeps the carry exactly and notes the distinction aloud. Keeper may wish to correct the index.
howItsDone: 'their sale is forbidden' (abolished under Pius V after Trent): confirm.
'With faults and hard words on more than one side': deliberately even-handed; confirm.
